title: Feature Flag and Staged Rollout Service
summary: Evaluate targeting rules and percentage rollouts locally at high QPS with fast global kill switches.
statement:
Design a feature flag and dynamic configuration platform used by backend services, web apps, and mobile clients across an organization.

Functional requirements:
- Engineers create boolean or multivariate flags, define targeting rules by tenant, user attribute, or explicit allowlist, and ramp percentage rollouts gradually.
- Server and client SDKs evaluate flags with negligible latency and continue working even if the feature flag service is unreachable.
- Toggling a kill switch or updating a rollout rule propagates to active SDK instances worldwide within a few seconds.
- Record an audit history of every rule change with one-click rollback to a previous version.

Scale to assume:
- 50,000 active flags across 2,000 internal services and client apps.
- 15 million flag evaluations per second across the fleet, compared with about 20 rule edits per minute.
- 250,000 connected server SDK instances and millions of active browser and mobile sessions.
hints: At 15 million evaluations per second, what happens to latency and availability if every `isEnabled` check makes a network call to a central service?
When a flag ramps from `10%` to `25%`, how do stateless app servers assign the same user to the same bucket without storing per-user assignments or flipping users who were already enabled?
Server SDKs need full rulesets, whereas mobile and browser clients are untrusted—how should rule delivery and evaluation differ between the two?
expectations: Clarifies consistency window for kill switches (eventual propagation within a few seconds), SDK evaluation latency target (sub-millisecond in-process), and server versus client SDK privacy requirements.
Separates the control plane (CRUD API, validation, audit history, relational store) from the read/distribution data plane so control-plane outages never block live traffic.
Evaluates rules locally in memory inside server SDKs rather than making per-request RPCs, seeding from a local disk snapshot or code-defined default on cold start.
Propagates immutable versioned ruleset snapshots via CDN-cached blobs paired with lightweight streaming invalidations (`SSE` or WebSockets) over regional relay nodes with jittered reconnects.
Computes sticky, monotonic percentage rollouts deterministically with `hash(flag_key + salt + subject_id) % 10000` so ramping a threshold never flips already-enrolled users.
Pre-evaluates flags for a specific user context on an edge endpoint for browser and mobile SDKs so sensitive tenant allowlists and unreleased targeting rules are never exposed in client bundles.
Stores immutable configuration versions with actor, diff, and optional approval metadata to support instant atomic rollback.
